title: Reading a Recorded Prefix
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine on Boolean symbols with state set $Q$, let $T$ be a tag set, let $u:T\times\{\text{blank},0,1\}\to T$ be a tag update rule, and let $S$ be the state set of a two-work-tape seeking machine with designated states $s_0,s_1$. For a Boolean input $x$, configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, tag $\tau\in T$, and four-work-tape record-alphabet configuration $d$, suppose the control of $d$ is the entry control and tape $0$ of $d$ agrees, at every offset from $-1$ through the joined-record length, with the field encoding of $c$ and $\tau$; suppose also that all other work tapes of $d$ are blank. If $w$ is the binary-digit encoding of the input-head position of $c$, the record-processing machine has a run of exactly $6|w|+17$ steps from $d$ to the snapshot whose control is at the position-skip stage, whose position-field head is shifted by $2$, and whose two buffers both contain $w$. Before the final step the run visits neither verdict state, and every work-tape head remains within distance $L+1$ of its initial position, where $L$ is the length of the joined field encoding.
hypotheses_covered: M is a k-work-tape Boolean Turing machine
u is a tag update rule
seek is a two-work-tape machine with designated start and finish states
x is a Boolean input; c is a configuration on x; τ is a tag
d is a four-work-tape record-alphabet configuration with entry control
tape 0 of d satisfies RecordAt for cfgRecord(s,c,τ)
every other work tape of d is blank
caveat: The statement uses the record encoding, entry control, and snapshot constructions defined in the formal snippet; the parameter s is implicit in the record hypothesis.
